title: Kumamoto earthquake kills at least 34 and causes severe damage in the region
summary: The earthquake, followed by aftershocks, caused explosions, collapses, service cuts, and disrupted transportation and industry, mobilizing authorities in rescue and humanitarian assistance efforts.

title: United States resumes bombings against Iran and tensions escalate in the Middle East
summary: US attacks resume as Iran claims to have killed US military personnel, raising the risk of a regional escalation.

title: Japanese Prime Minister announces reduction of consumption tax on food to 1% for two years
summary: The measure, which will take effect in April 2027, aims to alleviate inflationary pressure but draws criticism for its fiscal impact and raises doubts about its temporary nature.

title: Police search homes of two Hiroshima Carp players in investigation
summary: Baseball players Yano and Maekawa were subject to searches by Hiroshima police, and the club stated it will take the case seriously.

title: Yokohama mayor found guilty of workplace harassment by independent committee
summary: The committee determined that Mayor Yamanaka used his authority to pressure and denigrate municipal employees, creating a toxic work environment.

title: Sumo raises entry fees, wrestlers' salaries, and doubles championship prize
summary: Starting next year, the Sumo Association will increase the salaries of rikishi and the prize for the tournament winner to 20 million yen.

title: Former South Korean national football coach apologizes to parliament for World Cup failure
summary: Hong Myung-bo appeared before a parliamentary hearing to apologize for not meeting the country's expectations in the World Cup.

title: Figure skating pair 'Rikuryu' presents their first ice show
summary: The duo, known for their success in competitions, debuted as producers of a skating show, sharing the challenges of the project.

title: Court orders Japanese state to compensate victims of Anrakura farm fraud
summary: The Osaka court found that the government did not act adequately to prevent harm to investors in the wagyu cattle investment scheme.

title: Former executive of trademark trading company indicted for 784 million yen tax evasion
summary: The Tokyo prosecutor's office accused the former representative of hiding income from stock sales, in one of the largest income tax evasion cases.

title: China replaces Director of Foreign Ministry's Asian Affairs Department due to informal style
summary: The new director will be the former ambassador to Mongolia, amid speculation about changes in Chinese foreign policy.

title: Chinese Communist Party to hold key plenary meeting in October
summary: The plenum is expected to address internal discipline issues and possible adjustments to the leadership, in a context of anti-corruption efforts.

title: Electricity and gas rates drop in August due to increase in state subsidies
summary: Twelve energy companies reduced their prices for August consumption, easing the burden on households.

title: Vanraure Hachinohe club and local authorities agree to build new stadium
summary: The project aims to be completed by the 2034-35 season, with the goal of boosting football in the Aomori region.

title: Three Japanese political parties begin talks on possible merger
summary: The centrist, liberal, and Komeito parties presented an interim document with two options: full unification or electoral alliance.

title: Relatives of Henoko shipwreck victim file criminal complaint against eleven people
summary: The parents of the deceased student maintain that the captain was not solely responsible and seek to have more involved parties investigated.

title: Yen weakens to 163 per dollar and government considers currency intervention
summary: The yen's exchange rate fell sharply, sparking speculation about possible intervention by the Bank of Japan and the Ministry of Finance.
